items.previously_masked: This was invisible until 2026-08-25 because the test aborted on observed_multiome_integration first. It is a third scimilarity item, distinct from the open admission_blocking one.
items.resolution: Sanctioned schema evolution, not drift. Reclassified real_disagreement -> test_stale. Versioning past v1 is established practice here: 12 of 239 distinct schema_version strings under config/ are non-v1, including a v3 and a v4. All three scimilarity v2 files are STRICT SUPERSETS of the shape shared by every v1 peer, nested included, checked against all 62 / 103 / 61 peers rather than spot-checked: universal-in-v1 paths missing from v2 is NONE in every case. checkpoints.json v2 adds staged_model_contract; exposure_audit.json v2 adds frozen_fixture_contract and sealed_champion_eligible; development_crosswalk.json v2 adds 13 nested paths splitting the annotated training and test corpora, matching reference-only samples, and stating rules.{encoder_training,reference_only,sealed_timing}. Those are exactly what scimilarity uniquely needs as the census's only supervised-corpus model with a training/test/reference split and its only encoder_seen model. Fix was to widen the test's three accepted sets, not to migrate the bundle back, which would have deleted real recorded structure to satisfy a frozen list.
items.counter_argument_checked_and_discarded: No schema DEFINITION file exists for the v2 strings anywhere. But none exists for the v1 strings either -- the contract test's accepted sets are the only definition of these schemas in the repository. So the absence of a v2 definition is not evidence of drift; it is how every schema here works.
items.resolution_guard: test_versioned_audit_schemas_only_ever_add_fields in the contract suite, plus tests/unit/test_scimilarity_admission_and_schema_correction.py. Widening an accepted set is a laundering route unless something stops a bump being used to SHED a field, so every versioned successor is held to being a strict superset of the universal v1 shape, scimilarity is pinned as the only such bundle so a new one must be justified, and the specific structures that justified the bump are asserted present.

items.cause: Two bundle directories exist on disk but are absent from the census in config/evaluation/model_audit_bindings.toml: observed_multiome_integration and remaining_multimodal_families.
items.suggested_fix: Decide whether these two are census members. Either register them in model_audit_bindings.toml or move them out of the audit root.
items.resolution: Neither directory is a census member. Both are cross-cutting, task-scoped campaign disposition records whose subject models each already own a census bundle: observed_multiome_integration covers multivi, scglue, mofaplus and seurat_wnn; remaining_multimodal_families covers 13 more. Registering them as group bindings is provably self-defeating -- it re-resolves those 17 subjects away from their own directories and takes the audit root from 104 bundles / 2 orphans to 89 / 17, forcing expected_artifact_bundle_count down by 15. The aggregate rule has zero exceptions: all 17 group bindings have no member owning its own directory, which is exactly what these two invert. Reclassified from real_disagreement to test_scope_defect and fixed by scoping the audit root on species, declared in config/evaluation/model_audit_bindings.toml as non_census_record_directories with a [non_census_record_rules] contract. No bundle, record or base registry file was edited to achieve this.
items.resolution_guard: tests/unit/test_non_census_record_directories.py exercises the contract suite's real assert_non_census_record_dir against synthetic directories and proves each abuse is flagged rather than skipped: a record dir that grows a member file, one with no disposition record, one naming a grouped model_id (the laundering route -- hiding a real family as a record), one naming no registry model at all, one shadowing a census bundle id, and one whose named subject has no directory. It also pins that the aggregate rule has zero exceptions and that removing the declaration makes both directories fail again, so the scoping narrows nothing.

items.correction_to_the_working_hypothesis: admission_blocking is NOT true because of encoder_seen. The admission blocker is the missing ModelExecutionContract binding adapter, runtime, checkpoint, preprocessing, licences, corpus authorities and executable task. encoder_seen appears only in the blocker's final sentence, as a champion-eligibility statement. Two different gates: scimilarity is champion-ineligible because of encoder_seen and admission-blocked because of the missing contract, and clearing one would not clear the other. A reader conflating them would think admitting scimilarity requires resolving its exposure class, which is a different and much harder problem.

Second because it is not true in the sense the field means: the record checks two paths and they now differ. config/tasks/observed_multiome.toml is still absent while config/evaluation/observed_multiome_task.toml is present, and that asymmetry is deliberate -- the capabilities file states the task is kept outside config/tasks so it cannot mutate the frozen global census. items.no_status_conflict_existed: observed_multiome_task.toml status='candidate' and family_native_tournament.toml [task.observed_multiome] status='planned_registration' describe different axes. TaskSpec document status takes only {candidate, blocked}; tournament task status takes only {active, planned_registration, planned_activation_audit, compound}. Disjoint sets, and rna_conditioned_atac and variant_to_regulation each carry both at once. Nothing was made to yield.
items.token_regrounded_not_lifted: NO_TASKSPEC became TASKSPEC_EXECUTION_BLOCKED in the status and all four per-model gates, with the surviving conjuncts byte-identical and asserted so by test. The blocker now closes from the standalone TaskSpec's own admission_gates[0] and from the development gate's five prohibitions -- a stronger authority than absence.

items.suggested_fix: Report only, per the team lead. Whether the walk should be widened to recognise the flat-map shape is a separate conversation with the user.
items.decision_20260825: Team lead reviewed and declined to widen the walk now. 1 stale in 175, concentrated in 7 disposition-style records, does not justify changing a contract test that touches every lane mid-campaign. Recorded as a standing recommendation so the argument survives for whoever picks it up.
argument_for_widening_when_it_is_schedul: It would immediately surface the one live stale pin it cannot currently see: corgi_plus/release_disposition_20260824.json pinning pyproject.toml at fd298c3d..., live b8d0d84e....

It would have caught both observed_multiome_integration and remaining_multimodal_families drifting on config/models/multimodal_integration.toml days earlier. Both went stale silently because the walk cannot see a flat {path: digest} map, and the drift only surfaced when their own validators were run by hand on 2026-08-25.

The 23 percent gap is not spread thinly across the tree. It is concentrated in exactly the kind of file that pins many authorities at once, which is where a single upstream edit does the most silent damage.
The shape change is small: recognise a dict whose every value is a 64-hex digest and whose key resolves to a repo file, in addition to the existing path/sha256 sibling pair.
items.cost_of_widening: It would add 175 live pins to a test that already fails on 13 stale ones, so it should be sequenced after the stale-pin cascade in config/campaigns/stale_pin_refresh_plan_20260825.json is paid, not before.
items.worked_example_of_the_migration: The observed_multiome_integration re-grounding on 2026-08-25 did this migration for two pins as a by-product of doing the work correctly. Binding config/evaluation/observed_multiome_task.toml and config/evaluation/observed_multiome_development_gate.toml as proper {path, sha256} pairs inside task_gate, rather than as flat-map entries, put them into the contract walk: 196 -> 198 checked pins, both passing on the first run. That is the shape the widening should produce. The migration is per-record and mechanical -- rewrite {relative_path: digest} as a list or object of {path, sha256} -- it needs no change to the contract test, and it pays for itself immediately because the walk starts checking the pin the moment the shape is right. A record can be migrated on its own schedule by whoever next touches it, so the 175 do not have to move together.
items.two_routes: Either widen the walk to recognise the flat-map shape in one change (sequenced after the 13-pin cascade), or migrate records to the {path, sha256} shape incrementally as they are edited. The second needs no contract-test change and is already underway at 2 of 175.

items.test: (not a test) the suite's failure reporting understates how much is wrong
items.cause: unittest reports the first failing assertion in a method and stops, so a method with several wrong assertions is counted once. Three instances surfaced on 2026-08-25 alone: blockers == [] sitting behind admission_blocking in the scimilarity test; remaining_multimodal_families sitting behind observed_multiome_integration in the audit-bundle completeness test, which aborts on the alphabetically first offender; and scimilarity's three -v2 schema strings sitting behind both of those.
items.consequence: The failing-test count in this register is a FLOOR, not a measure. Each entry can hide further defects that only appear once the first is fixed, and in every case today the hidden one was substantive rather than cosmetic. Do not read a count of N as N problems.
items.suggested_fix: Report only. If it ever matters, the audit-bundle and scimilarity tests could collect offenders and assert once at the end instead of aborting, which is how the census re-derivations were done by hand today.

When another lane resolved test_model_census_maps_exactly_to_audit_bundles on 2026-08-25 and correctly shrank the register, the copy and the constant disagreed and the gate reported the campaign's own unit tests as new failures.

register_hygiene_lessons.right_fix: Derive the test fixture from the constant so the two cannot diverge.
register_hygiene_lessons.generalises_to: Any check that restates its subject rather than reading it: duplicated digests, duplicated counts, duplicated expected-failure lists, a test asserting a value the code also defines. The duplicate is correct exactly until someone else does the right thing.
